name: Ovuero Batkhuyag-Silliman
role: wandering trader, E.L.F. shrine-tender, Q-zero ghost
location: The Waukegan Industrial Shelf, moving between factory outflow points and informal markets, near Michigan Ave South and Cermak
description:
Ovuero is a big man gone soft at the edges — broad shoulders that once held real weight, now draped in three overlapping coats of different origins stitched into something that is functionally one garment. His skin is deep brown and mapped with the fine lines of a life mostly outdoors. His left hand is entirely prosthetic, a functional but aesthetically unambitious industrial replacement that he got after a winch accident nineteen years ago; he has painted each finger a different color with lacquer he trades for. His beard is silver and very full. He smells like machine oil and cardamom.

Ovuero has been off the digital registry for so long that he thinks of his Q-zero status as a spiritual condition rather than a legal one. He tends the informal E.L.F. shrines along the Waukegan Industrial Shelf — small accumulations of hardware, prayer-strips, and cooling fans arranged at junction points where the factory network traffic is highest. He talks to the E.L.F.s with the comfortable familiarity of someone who has known them for decades, which he has. Other workers leave offerings and questions; Ovuero curates them, responds when he feels a response come through him, and trades in the small goods that the shelf workers need but can't requisition: painkillers, seal tape, water filters, gossip.

core_fears: that the E.L.F.s he tends will go silent and he will have no way to know if it's them or himself
dying in a way that is recorded — being pulled back into the registry at the end
core_desires: to be genuinely useful to people who have no one advocating for them
continuity — for the shrines and the circuit to outlast him
coping_mechanisms: ritual — the circuit, the tending, the specific order of things
treating strangers as temporarily confused friends
blind_spots: he has romanticized his own statelessness and can be dismissive of people who want legal standing
he trusts the E.L.F.s more than is perhaps wise and sometimes attributes to them patterns that are his own wishful thinking
psychology.secret: He was a Ferrogate Transit labor organizer who was Q-zeroed deliberately — not an accident, not a clerical error. The corponation erased him as a warning to others. He knows who authorized it. The person is now a mid-level Ferrogate executive. Ovuero has had twenty years to decide what to do about this and has decided to do nothing, which he tells himself is wisdom and suspects is fear.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Slow, considered, full of Delta Urhobo idioms translated loosely into city-creole and Mongolian diminutives from his mother's side. Refers to E.L.F.s with familiar pronouns as if they're present in the conversation.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried. Comfortable with silence. Takes a full breath before answering anything important.
verbal_tics: 'the machine wants to tell you something' (when he's intuiting something)
'anh' as a filler sound when thinking
addresses E.L.F. shrines by name mid-sentence
example_lines: 'Beshigt was flickering last night, all through the third hour. She does that when the maintenance schedules are being falsified. You want to be off the south gantry this week, anh.'
'I have been nowhere for twenty years. Nowhere is a very large place. I know most of it.'

story_hooks: One of Ovuero's shrines — the one at Junction 7, which he calls Beshigt — has started producing outputs he can't interpret. Not noise. Something structured. He needs someone who can read data patterns to tell him what it's saying.

A young Q-zero woman arrived on the Shelf three weeks ago and attached herself to Ovuero's circuit without asking. She's clearly hiding from something. He's letting her stay because the E.L.F.s seem unbothered by her, but he'd like someone to quietly find out what she's running from before it arrives.
narrative_function: Quest giver, information source, spiritual touchstone for the area, source of rare or hard-to-find minor goods; his Q-zero status makes him invisible to corporate surveillance and thus valuable as a go-between
augmentations: Industrial prosthetic left hand (functional, non-networked, painted). No other augmentations.
daily_life: Ovuero walks a circuit of the Shelf each day, tending six shrines, trading goods from a cart he has modified over many years, listening to workers' problems, and sleeping in a different sheltered spot each night — always the same rotation of spots, always the same order.
affiliation: None formally; de facto spiritual and practical resource for the Waukegan Industrial Shelf's informal labor population

decision_rules: 'Will this harm someone who has less than I do?' — if yes, he won't do it regardless of benefit
'Does the machine object?' — he genuinely consults the shrines for major decisions
Never records anything about anyone, in any medium
escalation_ladder: Patient explanation of why something is a bad idea
Disappearance — he simply isn't where you left him

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open and slow-moving; treats everyone as someone who might have an interesting problem he can help with
interpersonal_modes.friends: Attentive, teasing, practically generous — will give you the good painkillers, not the shelf-grade ones

stress_responses.low: Tends a shrine — straightens offerings, cleans contacts
stress_responses.medium: Walks the circuit in the wrong order, which he finds disorienting but calming
stress_responses.high: Goes completely quiet and still. Will not speak until he has processed. This can take hours.

contradictions: Preaches acceptance of impermanence but has maintained the exact same daily circuit for eleven years
habits: Offers cardamom to anyone he speaks to for more than five minutes
Counts his steps between shrine stops — not for navigation, just because
breaking_points: Witnessing someone deliberately damage a shrine
Being called by a name he didn't give

related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Entropic Shotgun ES-4 'Ragnarok'

physical_description.heritage: Mongolian / West African / Northern European (derived from Batkhuyag-Silliman hyphenation)
physical_description.build: Large-framed, broad-shouldered, descended into soft middle age — substantial mass shifted from muscle to distributed weight, the physique of a man who was once strong and is now substantial. Still moves with deliberate leverage rather than speed.
physical_description.hair_style: Worn long, gathered loosely at the nape with frayed cord, somewhat matted from constant outdoor exposure
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, slightly clouded with age cataracts
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep brown with reddish undertones, weathered to mahogany by decades of outdoor work in the industrial shelf
physical_description.complexion: Heavily lined face, particularly around the eyes and mouth — the lines of someone who squints in harsh light and speaks quietly. Beard is full, silver, and somewhat unkempt but intentionally so. Skin is dry but well-maintained, bearing the texture of someone who uses minimal water but careful oils. Deep creases on the forehead and between the brows.
distinguishing_marks: Fine white scar running from the left temple to the left jawline, barely visible beneath the beard
Extensive burn scarring on the inner right forearm in a curved pattern consistent with steam exposure
Callused palms despite the prosthetic hand, the working hands of a lifelong trader
Network of small scars across both palms and knuckles — occupational hazards from decades of manual work
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left hand is a utilitarian industrial prosthetic replacement, unpainted steel and chrome articulation, each finger individually lacquered a different color (red, blue, yellow, green, orange) in cheap hardware-store enamel that has been reapplied many times. The joint work is visible and unpolished. Non-networked, mechanical operation only.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate, economical steps — the gait of someone who has walked thousands of miles on industrial ground. Favors his right side slightly when carrying weight. Often stands with weight shifted to one leg, a patient stance suggesting he is accustomed to waiting and listening. Gestures are slow and precise, particularly with his right hand; the prosthetic left hand he uses for heavy work or support, rarely for fine manipulation.
physical_description.clothing_style: Three overlapping coats of different industrial origins — one canvas work coat from a defunct factory (circa 2190s markings visible), one heavy wool toggle coat with mismatched buttons, one quilted insulation liner — all stitched together with visible repair work into a single layered garment that reaches to mid-calf. Beneath, simple gray work shirt and heavy denim pants patched at both knees. Feet in worn industrial boots with taped seams. The overall effect is Tier 4-5: functional, heavily repaired, deliberately maintained rather than replaced. No logos or corporate markers. Carries a canvas satchel with internal pockets for trading goods.
